body.statement: Can \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\) be realized so that, for every \(c\in\mathcal C_R\), its output \(c'\in\mathcal U_R\) satisfies \(2N_{c'}\ge2N_c\) and \(f_{c'}(n_B,n_S)\ge f_c(n_B,n_S)\) simultaneously for all \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), with equality conditions tracked in both directions?
body.justification: A positive answer would collapse the finite affine envelope to a closed all-resolution formula and expose the true extremal mechanism.
body.gap: Singhal's pure-profile reduction does not preserve a chosen common bivariate fiber, and the current catalog theorem bounds residual size without purifying residual shape.
body.consumer: Designers could compute the optimal rectangle in closed form for arbitrary \(R\), eliminating catalog enumeration in large experiments.
